AnomalyDetectRequest.description:
Run IsolationForest over recent telemetry.

The model is fitted per application on a feature matrix built from recorded
fields only. There is no target label, so the fit is unsupervised and the
"expected band" comes from the same window's percentiles.
AnomalyDetectRequest.title: AnomalyDetectRequest

feature_importance_proxy.title: Feature Importance Proxy
feature_importance_proxy.description: Per-feature deviation magnitude, not a fitted importance score

is_resolved.title: Is Resolved
is_resolved.description: true resolves the anomaly, false reopens it

AnomalyResolveRequest.description:
Resolve or reopen one anomaly.

A single field because resolution is the only mutable thing about a detected
anomaly: the measurement that produced it is a record, and editing it would
make the evidence disagree with the row it was meant to justify.
AnomalyResolveRequest.title: AnomalyResolveRequest

Aggregate of an answer evaluation. Deterministic and judge columns are
kept apart so the UI can never present a judge number as a measured one.
AnswerEvaluationSummary.title: AnswerEvaluationSummary

expires_at.description: Optional expiry. A key with none never expires; revocation is the control.

ApiKeyCreate.title: ApiKeyCreate

key_prefix.description: First 12 characters; never enough to authenticate

ApiKeyOut.description:
One key's metadata. Deliberately has no plaintext field.

``is_active`` is derived rather than stored: it is ``revoked_at is None and
expires_at is in the future``, and deriving it means an expired key stops
reading as usable without a background job having to run to notice. That
also makes this schema un-validatable from a row, for the same reason as
:class:`OrganizationOut` -- the field has no column behind it.
ApiKeyOut.title: ApiKeyOut

ApplicationStats.description:
Everything the per-application statistics page shows, in one object.

Not a paginated shape: this is a single window's summary, and the totals
(``trace_count``, ``total_tokens``) describe the whole window rather than a
page of it. ``model_usage`` and ``time_series`` are complete for the window
too — paging them would make the totals and the breakdown describe different
populations.
ApplicationStats.title: ApplicationStats

BatchIngest.description:
Buffered batch flush from the SDK.

The SDK buffers client-side so instrumenting a request does not add a
synchronous HTTP round trip to the application's hot path.
BatchIngest.title: BatchIngest

ClaimEvaluation.description: One extracted claim and whether the context supports it.
ClaimEvaluation.title: ClaimEvaluation

last_flush_at.title: Last Flush At
last_flush_at.description: ISO-8601 time of the last flush attempt

CollectorStatus.description:
Collector counters plus the current queue depth.

``queue_depth`` against ``queue_capacity`` is the pair to watch: depth pinned
at capacity means writes are arriving faster than the flush loop persists
them, and the gap is going to ``dropped`` rather than to a slower ingest.
CollectorStatus.title: CollectorStatus

CompareRequest.description:
Two recorded runs, and the size of a drop worth calling a regression.

``max_regression_pct`` is a threshold on the *recorded* relative change, not
a tolerance the report adjusts to produce a verdict: setting it to 0 flags
any movement at all, which is what you want when the baseline is a
published number other people are relying on.
CompareRequest.title: CompareRequest

ConfigDifference.description:
A recorded, factual difference between two runs' configurations.

Only keys that actually changed appear here — RAGOps never speculates
about causes beyond what the two configs literally say.
ConfigDifference.title: ConfigDifference

key_prefix.description: First 12 characters; never enough to authenticate

key.title: Key
key.description: Shown once. Store it now; it cannot be retrieved again.

CreatedApiKey.description:
A newly minted key, carrying its plaintext exactly once.

``key`` is populated from the value ``generate_api_key()`` returned and is
never readable from the database afterwards. Losing it is not a bug to
report: the operator who has not copied it revokes the key and mints
another.
CreatedApiKey.title: CreatedApiKey

EvalExample.description:
One labelled query in a retrieval evaluation dataset.

``relevant_documents`` holds document ids as they appear in the knowledge
base (``Document.external_id``), so a dataset stays valid across re-ingestion.
EvalExample.title: EvalExample

GenerationIn.description:
An LLM generation attached to a trace.

Token counts may be supplied by the caller (Ollama returns exact counts) or
omitted, in which case the server derives them from ``prompt``/``completion``
with the deterministic counter. The server never invents them.
GenerationIn.title: GenerationIn

IndexResponse.description:
What an index build actually produced.

``dimension`` is null until the index exists, because there is no embedding
dimension to report for an index that was not built — reporting the
configured model's dimension would be a guess about a computation that has
not happened.
IndexResponse.title: IndexResponse

ModelComparison.description: One row of the cost/quality scatter plot.
ModelComparison.title: ModelComparison

OrganizationCreate.description:
A company to onboard.

``name`` is unique platform-wide, which makes it the natural human handle
for "the org I already created" -- a client can test for the collision before
sending instead of having to interpret a 409. ``slug`` is optional and
derived from the name when omitted, because it exists for humans to read and
nothing resolves against it.
OrganizationCreate.title: OrganizationCreate

OrganizationOut.description:
One organization, as returned by every read.

``num_applications`` and ``num_api_keys`` are counts of rows that already
exist, not figures recomputed from telemetry, so they are cheap and exact.

Not ``model_validate``-able off a row: the two counts are aggregates the
model has no column for. :func:`app.api.v1.organizations.to_out` builds one
explicitly, which is why the mismatch is declared here rather than
discovered at the first request.
OrganizationOut.title: OrganizationOut

RagQueryRequest.description:
One demo question.

``top_k`` and ``application`` are optional overrides; leaving them unset
uses the configured pipeline defaults, which is what makes this endpoint a
faithful demo rather than a second, differently-configured pipeline.
RagQueryRequest.title: RagQueryRequest

RagQueryResponse.description:
The answer, its sources, and what it cost.

``usage`` distinguishes the three token counts the pipeline actually
distinguishes: what the model was sent, what it produced, and what the
retrieved context alone occupied. Collapsing them loses the one number an
operator needs to tell "the model is verbose" from "we are stuffing the
prompt".
RagQueryResponse.title: RagQueryResponse

RecommendationGenerateResponse.description:
Result of a generation request.

``notes`` is not decoration. A response of ``generated: 0`` with no
explanation is indistinguishable from "we looked and found nothing to
improve", and those two are very different things to show a user. The note
is where the route says which one this is.

``rules_evaluated`` closes the remaining gap: it reports every rule that ran
and the measurement it looked at, including the ones that stayed below
their threshold. A caller can then see that "no recommendation" means "six
statistics were computed and none justified one", rather than having to
trust that something happened at all.
RecommendationGenerateResponse.title: RecommendationGenerateResponse

RetrievalEvaluationRequest.description:
Run retrieval metrics over a labelled dataset.

Either point at an existing ``application`` (which runs the real retriever)
or supply ``retrieved_document_ids`` per example to score a result set that
was produced elsewhere. The second form is what evaluates a production
trace log without re-running retrieval.
RetrievalEvaluationRequest.title: RetrievalEvaluationRequest

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: When the retrieval ran. Defaults to the server's insert time, which is correct for live traffic but collapses a backfilled or replayed batch into one instant. State it when replaying history.

RetrievalIn.description: A retrieval stage attached to a trace.
RetrievalIn.title: RetrievalIn

content.title: Content
content.description: Full text; truncated server-side for storage

RetrievedDocumentIn.description:
One ranked retrieval hit.

Per-stage scores are optional but recommended: they are what lets the trace
view explain a ranking, and what the duplicate-context detector keys on.
RetrievedDocumentIn.title: RetrievedDocumentIn

SpanIn.description: A timed stage inside a trace.
SpanIn.title: SpanIn

TimeSeriesPoint.description:
One bucket of a time series.

``bucket`` is ISO-8601 UTC. Metrics are ``None`` rather than 0 for empty
buckets so the UI can break the line instead of drawing a false drop to zero.
TimeSeriesPoint.title: TimeSeriesPoint
